kaigo-language-session-11-notes.heading: Distinguish task order from conditions for starting
paragraphs: ‘B after A’ and ‘do not use until confirmed’ require different reading perspectives. The former is sequence; the latter is an implementation condition. Finishing an earlier task does not establish that an intervening check or personal consent is complete.
When organizing possessions, distinguish what may be moved from where it will be checked afterward. Consent to moving magazines does not extend to photographs or every possession.

The empty-wheelchair training memo is a reading task about inspection-record checks and movement responsibilities. It does not teach resident transfer or repair methods. The reception evacuation-drill memo likewise does not give a complete actual-fire response procedure.
The following three documents were created for learning. Mark responsible people, prerequisites and unfinished tasks, and check that you are not adding unstated actions or permissions.

〜なければなりません expresses necessity or obligation; 〜てはいけません expresses prohibition. In ‘the date must be checked before submission,’ checking is required, not prohibited. Read to the sentence end and separate necessary from forbidden actions.

kaigo-reading-new-252.heading: Read agreed scope in organizing possessions
paragraphs:
Confirmation memo: organizing personal belongings
Before organizing the shelf, explain which items will move and where they will be returned.
Today the person consented only to placing magazines on another shelf. They do not want photographs moved.
Afterward, check the magazines’ location with the person. This memo contains no completion record.

Before work, explain the items to move and their return location. Today’s permission covers magazines only; the person does not request moving photographs. Separate the general explanation of organizing from this specific consent scope.
Checking the magazines’ location with the person is planned after the work. With no completion record in this memo, neither organizing nor checking can be reported as complete.

kaigo-reading-new-253.heading: Read prerequisites for empty-wheelchair training
paragraphs:
Management memo: wheelchair for training
Before training: the person responsible checks inspection records. Do not use until the records have been checked.
Movement plan: after the inspection-record check, move the empty wheelchair to the display area. No resident will ride in it.
Explanation: the instructor will separately explain brake and tire inspection methods.
Current state: the record check is not yet complete.
The condition is no use until the responsible person checks inspection records. This remains unfinished. Do not reinterpret it as completed inspection or movement.

After checking, the empty display wheelchair is moved, with no resident riding. An instructor will explain brake and tire checks separately; do not infer operating methods from this text and carry them out.

kaigo-reading-new-254.heading: Read the drill receptionist’s sequence
paragraphs:
Evacuation-drill reception memo: training only
A: receive the roster and notify the person responsible of receipt.
B: after A is complete, wait for the drill-start announcement.
C: after the announcement, record numbers at reception in the assembly area.
This memo practices reception duties. In an actual fire, follow facility emergency procedures.
After A’s roster receipt and notification to the responsible person, B waits for the start announcement. C’s count recording follows the announcement, not immediately after receiving the roster.
This practices drill reception duties, not every firefighting or assisted-evacuation step. In an actual fire, follow facility emergency procedures and necessary instructions.

kaigo-language-session-11-terms.heading: Document-reading vocabulary reference
paragraphs: This list is a reference. Select words needed for today’s documents; it is not an assignment to memorize everything at once.
条件（じょうけん） — A requirement to meet before starting or proceeding. Distinguish it from sequence alone.
手順（てじゅん） — A description of what to do and in which order.
同意（どうい） — Acceptance of the specific explained content. It does not necessarily include another task.
私物（しぶつ） — Personal belongings. Check with the person the scope of organizing or moving them.
点検（てんけん） — Checking equipment or similar items. Also distinguish reviewing records from actually performing inspection.
受領（じゅりょう） — Receiving an item or document handed over.
開始放送（かいしほうそう） — An announcement that a drill or similar activity is starting.
完了（かんりょう） — The state of a planned task being finished. The existence of a plan alone does not establish completion.

kaigo-language-session-12-notes.heading: Record preparation, explanation, replies and implementation separately
paragraphs: Preparing items, hearing explanations, making choices and implementing an activity or assistance are separate events. Plans or supplies alone do not justify recording consent or completed support.

Activity preparation begins with asking whether the person wants to participate. Choose cards with those who wish to join, then proceed to further checks. Finished selection and an activity having started are not the same state.

These records do not specify individual water temperature, fluid amounts, swallowing or posture instructions, or break length. Do not fill absent conditions with general numbers or self-chosen methods. For actual support, check the person’s condition and current plan.

In the following documents, distinguish completed actions such as ‘explained’ and ‘started’ from future actions such as ‘planned’ and ‘will check.’ Even when a time appears, check whether this is a schedule or an implementation record.

kaigo-reading-new-255.heading: Conditions from participation wishes to card preparation
paragraphs:
Activity-preparation procedure memo
Before starting, ask whether the resident wants to participate.
Choose cards with those who want to join, then check the number selected.
Finally, tell them the start time. Also explain that they can tell a worker if they want to stop partway through.
Card selection alone must not be recorded as the activity having started.
First ask participation wishes, choose cards with those interested, check the number and then give the start time. Also explain that the person can express a wish to stop partway through.
Completed card selection does not record an activity start. Keep asking wishes separate from confirming actual participation or commencement.

kaigo-reading-new-256.heading: Ready towels and remaining checks
paragraphs:
Bathing-plan handover
Morning: the person heard the explanation of the afternoon bathing plan and wants to answer later about participation.
Preparation: towels are ready. The responsible person will next check the bathroom environment and the person’s current condition.
Handover: discuss today’s response after wishes and checking results are known.
The completed parts are the morning plan explanation and towel preparation. The person wants to reply later; they have not decided to participate in bathing.

The responsible person still needs to check the bathroom environment and current condition. A response is discussed once wishes and results are known. Towels alone do not establish readiness of bathing conditions.

kaigo-reading-new-257.heading: Meal start times and unconfirmed outcomes
paragraphs:
Meal-time record
11:20: a worker explained the menu. The person asked to hear one dish’s name again.
11:25: after the question was answered, the meal began.
12:05: asking post-meal wishes is planned. Intake and current condition are absent from this record.
This record alone does not establish that everything was eaten or post-meal support is complete.

The menu was explained at 11:20 and the person asked to hear a dish name again. The question was answered before the meal began at 11:25. Preserve the order: explanation, request for repetition, answer, start.
12:05 is the planned time to ask post-meal wishes. Intake and current condition are not recorded, so this record cannot establish outcomes such as eating everything or completing post-meal support.

kaigo-language-session-12-terms.heading: Document-reading vocabulary reference
paragraphs: This list is a reference. Select words needed for today’s documents; it is not an assignment to memorize everything at once.
準備（じゅんび） — Arranging items and conditions needed for an upcoming action.
用意済み（よういずみ） — The work of preparing necessary items is already complete.
参加（さんか） — Joining an activity. This differs from hearing an explanation.
献立（こんだて） — The combination of dishes served in a meal.
聞き直す（ききなおす） — Asking again about content that was unclear or similar information.
予定（よてい） — Intended future time or content of an action.
実施（じっし） — Actually carrying out a schedule or plan.
未記載（みきさい） — Information is not written in that document or field. It does not mean the event did not occur.

kaigo-language-session-13-notes.heading: Check notice audience, period, exceptions and purpose
paragraphs: For notices, first read the intended audience, effective period and changed location. Also check contacts for those who find the arrangement difficult and information in separate guidance. Do not expand a narrowly targeted notice into a rule for everyone or everything.

Separate a contact deadline from the day items must be brought. A family inquiry about displaying photographs does not establish the person’s wish to exhibit them. Check the specific items and personal wishes.

Even numbered text may describe distribution of handwashing materials rather than handwashing movements. Read title and purpose, then identify who checks the version, who marks words and who explains.
The next three notices are fictional learning scenes. Do not apply their periods or contacts as real facility rules. For actual actions, check your workplace’s latest guidance.

kaigo-reading-new-258.heading: Reception-change period and separately checked information
paragraphs:
Visitor notice: fictional facility
Reception change: from November 6 through November 9, visitor reception is at the east entrance. Normal reception resumes November 10.
Contact: if the east entrance is difficult to use, consult reception before visiting.
Phone: call reception during opening hours. Check those hours in separate guidance.

Use the east entrance November 6–9; normal reception resumes November 10. Anyone finding the east entrance difficult should consult reception before visiting. Preserve this notice’s audience and period.
Specific phone reception hours are absent from this notice. Check separate opening-hours guidance rather than adding imagined usual opening times.

kaigo-reading-new-259.heading: Photo-display contact deadline and personal wishes
paragraphs:
Preparing an exhibition
For families: if you have photographs you want displayed, contact the person responsible by October 2. Bring photographs after receiving confirmation.
For staff: also check the person’s display wishes. Do not decide from family contact alone.
This notice concerns photograph displays. Check other belongings’ rules separately.
By October 2, contact the person responsible if photographs are proposed for display. Bringing them follows confirmation, so do not change the contact deadline into a delivery deadline.
Staff also ask the person whether display is wanted. Family contact alone does not decide it, and rules for non-photographic belongings need separate checks.

kaigo-reading-new-260.heading: Separate training-material distribution from handwashing movements
paragraphs:
Handwashing-training material distribution memo
1. The person responsible checks the version currently to be used.
2. After version confirmation, distribute materials to participants.
3. Participants mark unfamiliar words. The instructor explains them.
This memo contains no handwashing-movement procedure. Practical work follows confirmed materials and instruction.
The responsible person checks the version; participants receive materials and mark unknown words; the instructor explains. Distribution follows version confirmation.

The three numbers allocate material-distribution tasks; they are not three handwashing actions. Practice follows checked materials and instruction. Do not create movements or disinfection conditions from this text.

kaigo-language-session-13-terms.heading: Document-reading vocabulary reference
paragraphs: This list is a reference. Select words needed for today’s documents; it is not an assignment to memorize everything at once.
掲示（けいじ） — Displaying guidance or similar information where people can see it.
来訪（らいほう） — Someone coming to visit a facility or similar place.
受付（うけつけ） — The desk handling arrivals, procedures or inquiries, or the work itself.
期限（きげん） — The final point by which an action must be completed. Check which action it concerns.
持参（じさん） — Bringing an item yourself, distinct from merely making contact.
版（はん） — A distinction between document content or revisions. Check the version currently in use.
配布（はいふ） — Distributing materials or similar items to those who need them.
印を付ける（しるしをつける） — Adding a mark to identify a noticed location or similar detail.

kaigo-language-session-14-notes.heading: Read tables by date, meal and responsibility
paragraphs: Read a menu table row by row, matching date with meal period. Distinguish staple food, side dish and dessert columns. なし and 梨 sound alike but differ according to written characters and the column.
In event plans, distinguish expected from actual attendance and staff preparation from the person choosing how to participate. A roster does not establish that everyone accepted the same role.
When a condition such as location changes, organize changed and unchanged details and ask wishes again. Creating a change notice differs from completing contact with family.
The following schedules are for learning. Explain one changed detail, one unchanged detail and one pending matter in each. Do not summarize planned entries as ‘everything confirmed.’

kaigo-reading-new-261.heading: Match date and meal columns and distinguish same-sounding words
paragraphs:
Menu-check memo: planned
September 12, lunch: staple = barley rice; side dish = steamed fish; dessert = apple.
September 12, dinner: staple = rice; side dish = tofu with thickened sauce; dessert = なし.
September 13, lunch: staple = bread; side dish = vegetable soup; dessert = 梨.
なし means no dessert in this dinner entry. 梨 means pear. Record actual serving separately.
September 12 lunch has steamed fish as the side dish; September 13 lunch has bread as the staple. September 12 dinner’s なし means no dessert; September 13 lunch’s 梨 means the fruit pear.
This is a planned menu. A dish name alone does not establish actual serving or personal intake. Keep implementation records separate from intake checks.

kaigo-reading-new-262.heading: Expected attendance, responsibilities and personal choices
paragraphs:
Read-aloud gathering preparation plan
Date/time: April 18,14:10–14:50. Location: library corner.
Expected attendance:8 residents and 2 workers. Record actual attendance after the event.
Responsibilities: Worker A prepares books; Worker B discusses seats with those interested.
Residents may choose reading, listening or not participating. A planned roster does not determine roles.
The event is planned for April 18,14:10–14:50 at the library corner. Eight residents and two workers make ten expected people; actual attendance is recorded afterward.
Worker A prepares books and B discusses seats with those interested. The person can read, listen or decline participation. A roster alone does not assign everyone a reading role.

kaigo-reading-new-263.heading: Location changes and unfinished contact
paragraphs:
Craft-exchange event change notice
The location changed from the courtyard to the indoor lounge. The start remains 15:20.
Worker A: contact families about the location change.
Worker B: ask residents whether they still want to attend after the change.
Worker C: prepare display cards. Family contact is not yet complete.
Only location changed, from courtyard to indoor lounge. The 15:20 start remains; do not add a time change.
Worker A contacts family, B asks participation wishes after the change, and C prepares cards. Family contact remains incomplete. A written change notice does not establish completed notification.

kaigo-language-session-14-terms.heading: Document-reading vocabulary reference
paragraphs: This list is a reference. Select words needed for today’s documents; it is not an assignment to memorize everything at once.
主食（しゅしょく） — A meal’s staple category, such as rice or bread. Match it to the table column.
副食（ふくしょく） — Side dishes eaten with the staple. Do not confuse it with the staple column.
梨（なし） — Pear, a fruit. The written character distinguishes it from なし meaning none.
参加予定（さんかよてい） — Expected participation recorded in a plan, separate from confirmed actual attendance.
担当（たんとう） — Responsibility for work or a check, or the person holding that responsibility.
変更（へんこう） — Changing some existing content or conditions. Check unchanged details too.
行事（ぎょうじ） — An event planned beforehand.
希望（きぼう） — Feelings about what the person wants to do or have done.

kaigo-language-session-15-notes.heading: Separate dates across midnight, discovery, cause and response
paragraphs: Read night-shift dates and times together. Shortly after midnight on the following day comes after 22:00 on the previous day. Do not order by clock numbers alone. Check the date boundary when considering elapsed time.
Finding a damaged item differs from knowing who damaged it or how. Keep observed condition separate from judgments about cause; describe unconfirmed causes as unconfirmed.
Records of contact, form entry or requests for inspection or replacement do not prove that the recipient read, agreed or completed action. Check the recipient and outcome separately.

The next three records are fictional exercises for reading workplace documents. Separate confirmed facts, unknown causes and requests with unconfirmed results. Check that responsibility is not assigned to someone without evidence.

A schedule’s ‘times per period’ expresses frequency over a set interval. ‘Materials updated once every three weeks’ in a learning notice differs from once a week. Start time, duration and frequency are separate information. This example concerns document updates, not intervals for rounds or condition checks.

kaigo-reading-new-264.heading: Compare scheduled times with recorded completion
paragraphs:
Day-shift task check sheet
09:40(planned): organize materials. Actually finished at 09:55.
10:10(planned): check the notice. No start record yet.
12:10–12:40(planned): break. Record changes if any.
14:30(planned): report check results to the person responsible. Identify unconfirmed items as unconfirmed.
Material organization was planned for 09:40 and actually finished at 09:55. The 10:10 notice check has no start record, so it cannot be described as already inspected.
The 12:10–12:40 break is planned for 30 minutes.14:30 is also a planned report time, not proof that every item will be complete. Unconfirmed items remain described as unconfirmed when reporting.

kaigo-reading-new-265.heading: After midnight the next day and an unchecked recipient
paragraphs:
Night-shift contact-check memo
October 22,22:50: received a change to the following morning’s visit plan.
October 23,00:20: entered the change in the handover field.
October 23,06:15(planned): explain details to the day-shift worker responsible.
The entry is complete, but whether the day-shift worker has read it remains unchecked.
One hour 30 minutes elapsed from receipt at 22:50 on October 22 to entry at 00:20 on October 23.00:20 is after the date boundary, not before 22:50.
The handover entry is complete, but whether the day-shift worker read it remains unconfirmed. The 06:15 explanation is planned. Entry alone does not complete explanation to the recipient.

kaigo-reading-new-266.heading: Observed damage versus unknown cause and replacement
paragraphs:
Damaged-supply report
Discovery: at 08:35, a worker found a cracked table-clock cover in the lounge.
Immediately preceding circumstances: the previous user and how it cracked remain unknown.
Response: reported to the person responsible and requested inspection and replacement. No completion notice yet.
Additional entries: add only confirmed facts.

At 08:35, the worker found a crack in the table-clock cover in the lounge. The previous user and process of damage remain unchecked. Do not invent a cause or responsibility, such as someone dropping it.
Reporting and requests for inspection and replacement are complete, but completion has not been communicated. Add only confirmed facts; do not assume replacement is finished.

kaigo-language-session-15-terms.heading: Document-reading vocabulary reference
paragraphs: This list is a reference. Select words needed for today’s documents; it is not an assignment to memorize everything at once.
日勤（にっきん） — A shift mainly during daytime. Check exact hours with the workplace or schedule.
夜勤（やきん） — A shift including nighttime. If it crosses midnight, read date and time together.
翌朝（よくあさ） — The morning of the following day.
記入（きにゅう） — Entering necessary information in a document field or similar space.
発見（はっけん） — Finding a condition or event not previously noticed.
破損（はそん） — Damage such as part of an item cracking.
原因（げんいん） — What gives rise to a condition or event. Do not fill an unconfirmed cause with guesses.
追記（ついき） — Adding content to an existing record afterward.

kaigo-language-session-16-notes.heading: Hand over individual exceptions and revised timing
paragraphs: In transport tables, match time and return method for each person or code. Do not turn one person’s exception into everyone’s rule. Hand over information under checking within that person’s row. R1–R3 here are fictional codes.

Assembly and departure are separate times. Check old and new details before calculating differences. Even a corrected notice does not automatically mean the person heard, understood or consented to the new time.

‘It is quiet now’ at night expresses the person’s experience at that moment. It does not invalidate the earlier concern, establish that a noise cause was removed or show sleep continued until morning.
These are learning records for reading handovers. Match personal words, the time heard and the time reported. Do not add unstated causes or subsequent condition.

kaigo-reading-new-267.heading: Match return time and method to each code
paragraphs:
Transport-plan handover: fictional resident codes
Expected morning arrivals: three people,R1,R2 and R3.
Planned afternoon returns: R1 at 14:40 in the facility vehicle; R2 at 15:10 collected by family.
R3’s return time and method remain under checking. Do not report that everyone returns in the same vehicle.
Record actual arrivals and returns in separate fields.
Three arrivals are expected:R1,R2 and R3. R1 plans to return at 14:40 in the facility vehicle; R2 at 15:10 with family. Do not apply one person’s method to everyone.

R3’s return time and method remain under checking. Plans do not establish actual arrival or return; confirm results in separate fields. Do not connect fictional codes to abilities or life histories of real residents with similar identifiers.

kaigo-reading-new-268.heading: New assembly/departure times and explanation status
paragraphs:
Outing-plan change notice
Old plan: tomorrow, assembly 09:05, departure 09:15.
New plan: tomorrow, assembly 09:35, departure 09:50. Destination and accompanying worker are unchanged.
Check: the responsible person will explain the new times. Whether explanation is complete remains unconfirmed.
Collection arrangements are not stated here.
Use the new 09:35 assembly and 09:50 departure,15 minutes apart. Do not confuse assembly with departure or continue using the old 09:05 and 09:15 times.

Destination and accompanying worker are unchanged, but their specific names are absent. Completed explanation of new times remains unconfirmed, and collection arrangements are not recorded. A changed document does not mean the person has already heard and consented.

kaigo-reading-new-269.heading: Match timed statements with the report
paragraphs:
Nighttime communication record
21:40: the person said, ‘The corridor noise bothers me.’ Its cause is unconfirmed.
22:05: when the worker asked, the person said, ‘It is quiet now.’
22:10: both timed accounts and the unconfirmed cause were reported to the person responsible.
Subsequent sleep is absent from this record.

At 21:40 the person reported bothersome noise; at 22:05 they said it was quiet now. Preserve both experiences at their different times rather than erasing the earlier concern with the later statement.

At 22:10, both accounts and the unconfirmed cause were reported to the person responsible. Subsequent sleep is unrecorded, so neither resolution of the cause nor a good night’s sleep is established. This text also gives no diagnostic or treatment instructions.

kaigo-language-session-16-terms.heading: Document-reading vocabulary reference
paragraphs: This list is a reference. Select words needed for today’s documents; it is not an assignment to memorize everything at once.
送迎（そうげい） — Picking people up and taking them to or from their destinations.
到着（とうちゃく） — Reaching the intended destination.
帰宅（きたく） — Returning to one’s home.
集合（しゅうごう） — Gathering at an agreed location. This is a separate time from departure.
出発（しゅっぱつ） — Leaving a place to head toward a destination.
確認中（かくにんちゅう） — Information is currently being checked, not already finalized.
申し送り（もうしおくり） — Passing information needed for support to the next responsible worker or others.
睡眠（すいみん） — Sleeping. A statement that it is quiet does not establish sleep outcomes.

kaigo-gap-hand-legend.heading: Read the legend of commonly missed hand areas
paragraphs: A hand diagram using two shading intensities distinguishes commonly missed areas from especially commonly missed areas. Shading is not a measurement of microorganism numbers or the percentage of cleanliness achieved.

Palms and backs of hands are separate surfaces. One appearing washed does not confirm coverage between fingers, at fingertips or nails, thumbs and their bases, or wrists. Review both hands and the necessary areas together.
Unshaded areas are not guaranteed clean either. Check body-area names and hand surfaces. Do not interpret lighter shading as permission to omit an area or no shading as no need to wash.

This unit teaches the legend and commonly missed areas. Infection precautions require hand hygiene at appropriate times with appropriate methods. Confirm washing with running water and soap when dirt is visible; actual practice follows facility-trained methods and product instructions.

Learning comparison: a learner thinks clean-looking palms remove the need to check other surfaces. Do not infer the whole from one part. Check backs, between fingers, fingertips, thumbs and wrists too. The diagram alone cannot establish a germ-removal percentage.

155.title: Read procedural conditions and consent scope
objectives: Explain task order, implementation conditions and the person’s permitted scope separately.
Distinguish empty-equipment training from actual assistance and drill roles from emergency response.
155.context: Read conditions, timing, roles and the scope established by documents created for learning. Do not convert fictional times or rules into actual assistance instructions.
155.artCaption: Workers check procedures and conditions together. The picture does not show stair-movement or assisted-evacuation methods.

156.title: Read preparation separately from implementation outcomes
objectives: Distinguish preparation, explanation, choice, implementation and outcomes according to textual timing.
Communicate necessary checks without inventing absent care conditions or intake.
156.context: Read conditions, timing, roles and the scope established by documents created for learning. Do not convert fictional times or rules into actual assistance instructions.
156.artCaption: Discuss prepared items and checks still needed. Supplies alone do not establish completed support.

157.title: Check guidance periods, audiences and purposes
objectives: Organize notice audience, period, contact deadline and conditions for bringing items.
Do not reinterpret material-distribution steps as handwashing movements.
157.context: Read conditions, timing, roles and the scope established by documents created for learning. Do not convert fictional times or rules into actual assistance instructions.
157.artCaption: Two notices are compared. Check audiences and effective periods before communicating them.

158.title: Read menu and event plans row by row
objectives: Match date, meal and column, and distinguish なし from 梨 through context.
Separate planned attendance from personal choice and changed details from unfinished contact.
158.context: Read conditions, timing, roles and the scope established by documents created for learning. Do not convert fictional times or rules into actual assistance instructions.
158.artCaption: Workers check written information together. Confirm actual menus or responsibilities in the relevant text row.

159.title: Read records across midnight and unconfirmed causes
objectives: Order times across date changes and explain elapsed time.
Report discovery separately from cause and requests separately from completed responses.
159.context: Read conditions, timing, roles and the scope established by documents created for learning. Do not convert fictional times or rules into actual assistance instructions.
159.artCaption: Compare nighttime records including dates and times. Do not move old results into a new field.

160.title: Hand over exceptions and revised plans accurately
objectives: Match return methods to codes and old/new assembly and departure times.
Preserve personal statements at different times without adding absent causes or sleep outcomes.
160.context: Read conditions, timing, roles and the scope established by documents created for learning. Do not convert fictional times or rules into actual assistance instructions.
160.artCaption: Separate making a record from the responsible person checking the handover. The picture does not show transport or sleep outcomes.

161.title: Check hand-hygiene legends and areas
objectives: Explain that shading warns about commonly missed areas.
Check both hand surfaces and necessary areas without determining cleanliness or germ-removal percentage from a diagram alone.
161.context: Supplementary learning reads the legend of a color-coded hand diagram and considers commonly missed areas. Shading does not establish actual contamination or germ-removal percentage.
161.artCaption: A scene washing with running water and soap. It does not show the two-shade legend or confirm every stage.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-252.prompt: Which correctly reads consent scope and task state in the possessions memo?
options: Consent to organizing permits moving magazines and photographs.
Explain moving items first, but not return locations until afterward.
The memo records a completed check of magazine placement with the person.
Explain moving items and return locations beforehand; today’s consent covers magazines only. Completion is not recorded.
rationales: Photograph movement is not wanted. This expands magazine-only scope.
Return locations are also explained before organizing, not only afterward.
Checking is planned after work, not recorded as complete.
This separates advance explanation, current consent and absence of a completion record.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-252.reading:
Confirmation memo: organizing personal belongings
Before organizing the shelf, explain which items will move and where they will be returned.
Today the person consented only to placing magazines on another shelf. They do not want photographs moved.
Afterward, check the magazines’ location with the person. This memo contains no completion record.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-253.prompt: What is currently known about the training wheelchair?
options: The inspection-record check is complete, and a resident rode to the display area.
The record check is incomplete, but this memo gives every inspection method.
The record check is incomplete; the empty chair will move afterward. Inspection methods will be explained separately.
No resident rides, so there is no record-check condition.
rationales: The check is unfinished and no resident will ride. This changes both status and subject.
An instructor explains methods separately; the memo lacks the full procedure.
This preserves unfinished checking, the later plan and the empty-chair condition.
Even for empty equipment, no use until checking is explicitly required.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-253.reading:
Management memo: wheelchair for training
Before training: the person responsible checks inspection records. Do not use until the records have been checked.
Movement plan: after the inspection-record check, move the empty wheelchair to the display area. No resident will ride in it.
Explanation: the instructor will separately explain brake and tire inspection methods.
Current state: the record check is not yet complete.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-254.prompt: Which sequence and scope appear in the drill-reception memo?
options: Receive the roster and notify, wait for the start announcement, then record numbers afterward. This is reception training.
Record numbers immediately after receiving the roster, then wait for the announcement.
Wait for the announcement first and record numbers before receiving the roster.
A–C show techniques for transferring residents.
rationales: This preserves A/B/C order and the document’s drill-reception purpose.
Count recording follows the announcement. Immediate recording after receipt omits the waiting condition.
B follows completion of A, so waiting does not come first.
The content concerns roster receipt, waiting and count recording, not transfer techniques.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-254.reading:
Evacuation-drill reception memo: training only
A: receive the roster and notify the person responsible of receipt.
B: after A is complete, wait for the drill-start announcement.
C: after the announcement, record numbers at reception in the assembly area.
This memo practices reception duties. In an actual fire, follow facility emergency procedures.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-255.prompt: Which activity-preparation order and recording scope is appropriate?
options: Staff first choose everyone’s cards, start, then ask participation wishes.
Selecting cards with interested people establishes a confirmed activity start.
Decide card numbers first without checking nonparticipation choices.
Ask participation wishes, select with those interested, and check number and start time. Selection alone does not establish a start.
rationales: Ask wishes first and select with interested people, rather than staff choosing everything and asking only after starting.
Card selection is explicitly separate from activity commencement.
Check numbers of cards selected with interested people, without omitting participation wishes.
This preserves wishes and preparation order, including explanation that stopping partway through can be requested.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-255.reading:
Activity-preparation procedure memo
Before starting, ask whether the resident wants to participate.
Choose cards with those who want to join, then check the number selected.
